data.why: Every page fetches live from UniProt/PDBe/Europe PMC by accession or PDB code typed into a text box; there is no file upload anywhere in the app, and each page already ships a sensible hardcoded default (e.g. UniProt AC Q9NR09, PDB codes 9eii/9eij/9eih) that the agent can just click 'Fetch'/'Analyse' on.

goals: Find all PDB structures and associated literature (PMIDs) for a UniProt accession
List the UniProt protein entries, resolution/method, and bound ligands for one or more PDB codes
View ligand-protein interaction sites and inspect a ligand in a 2D viewer
Visualise transmembrane annotation (UniProt-derived and manually edited) on a 3D protein structure
Find homologous proteins and UniRef90/UniRef50 cluster members that have experimental structures
Align a PDB chain's sequence to its UniProt canonical sequence and inspect identity/coverage
Fetch SIFTS residue-numbering mappings for a PDB entry in DBREF format

review.summary: The tree is accurate and well built for the five pages it reached: the goal and phases match Haku's stated purpose, the labels are clean, and 11 sampled screens plus the independent replay back almost every node, with one miscount (24 written, 25 shown). It should not be filed yet because three of the eight README features are absent: Similar structures and the 3D viewer were never opened, and View interactions failed on this server's DNS.
